provenance.paper_title: MA-EgoQA: Question Answering over Egocentric Videos from Multiple Embodied Agents

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v2 (HTML full text) reviewed on 2026-08-30

representation_paths.memory_component: per-agent individual memory: VLM captions of each embodied agent's egocentric video stream, produced at fixed 10-minute intervals over the multi-day recording

evidence.paraphrase: Each agent's long egocentric video is compressed into natural-language captions at every 10-minute interval; these per-agent caption records are the modality-native perception converted into a persistent textual store that the second retrieval stage queries. Each caption is tied to its agent identity and its 10-minute window, so the originating video segment remains locatable.

The second retrieval stage issues agent-specific sub-queries, each pairing an agent identifier with a sub-question, and retrieves top-k entries from that agent's individual caption memory; the agent identifier acts as a metadata routing key on top of lexical similarity ranking.

representation_paths.memory_component: system-level shared event memory: 4W1H (When, What, Where, Who, How) event records synthesised by a central manager from the parallel per-agent captions

evidence.paraphrase: A centralised manager integrates the individual captions into system-level summaries by identifying key events and explicitly recording, for each event, the fields When, What, Where, Who and How. The result is a schematised spatio-temporal record that aligns several agents' viewpoints into one coherent global memory, distinct from the flat per-agent caption stream it is built from.

Answering runs a two-tier read: BM25 ranking over the system-level event memory returns top-n events, which condition agent-specific sub-queries into the lower per-agent tier; a score threshold filters the union before response generation. The two tiers form one hierarchical store rather than independent indexes.

derived.hybrid_relation: The system-level 4W1H event records and the per-agent caption records are deliberately linked (events index into the agents whose captions produced them) and are jointly supplied to the answer generator through the two-stage retrieval cascade.

adjudication_notes: Tier judged T1: the shared memory is fully precomputed from the recorded egocentric streams before question answering; at QA time the system only performs query-conditioned two-stage retrieval and threshold filtering over fixed items. No persistent memory content, metadata or organisation changes during inference, and no deployment feedback alters any write or retrieval policy.

The 10-minute-interval caption/summary integration is memory formation over the stream, not inference-time memory management, and therefore does not raise the tier under the guide's formation/inference boundary rule.

Both representation paths are textual by leaf, but the non-text-modality criterion is met at formation: the memory is derived entirely from multiple egocentric video streams, and video is the central persistent experience and the evaluation setting.

source_accessibility recorded as linked_recoverable because every record carries an agent identifier and a temporal window (the 4W1H 'When'/'Who' fields) that locate the originating video segment. The full text does not explicitly describe re-sampling video frames at answer time; if strict re-access is required, this field would drop to retained_not_accessible.
Evidence pointers taken from the arXiv HTML full text (Sections 5.1-5.2, Figure 5, Tables 2/5b). PDF page numbers were not resolved.

source_accessibility lowered from 'linked_recoverable' to 'retained_not_accessible' during merge review: the paper never states that video frames are re-accessed at answer time, and the guide forbids inferring a mechanism from field structure alone. The 4W1H Who/When fields index events but are not shown to return source video.
